Understanding the retry schedule helps when you tune timeouts. The client waits one second, then two, then four, and gives up after the fifth try. Total wait is thirty seconds at most, which should stay under the load balancer limit.

The queue is persistent: messages are written to disk before the broker acknowledges them. That costs a little throughput. If you can tolerate losing messages on a crash, the in-memory mode is faster.

Once a connection is established, the client sends a heartbeat every twenty seconds. If three heartbeats go unanswered, it closes the socket and reconnects. The delay between attempts grows each time up to a limit of one minute.
The sort function does not mutate the input, so the original first element stays where it was. It returns a new array. If you need in-place sorting for a very large list, use the sortInPlace variant.

CI secrets are masked in build logs, but a value printed in a different encoding could slip through. Avoid echoing them at all. If one leaks, rotate it right away and note the incident in the security channel.
